newsitem.title: USA: USDA OFFERS GSM-102 CREDITS TO SOUTHERN AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: USDA OFFERS GSM-102 CREDITS TO SOUTHERN AFRICA.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department said Tuesday it was offering $50 million in short-term export credit guarantees to 18 nations in Southern Africa for fiscal 1997.
The credits, thorugh the GSM-102 program, will be available on a first-come, first-served basis to exporters for sales of a wide ranges of goods to any of the nations.
Eligible nations were Angola, Botswana, Burundi, Lesotho, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Mazambique, Namibia, Rwanda, Sudan, Seychelles, South Africa, Swaziland, Tanzania, Zaire, Zambia and Zimbabwe.

Commodities eligible for export credit coverage were barley malt, 12 types of dairy products, feed grains, fish, shellfish, frozen or chilled meats, oilseeds, potatos, pulses, rice, solid woods, tallow, grease, lard, tree nuts, vegetable oils, wheat, wheat flour, semolina, wood pulp and wood chips.
Eligible vegetable oils were soy, sunflower, cottonseed, corn and peanut oils.
Oilseeds eligible for coverage were soybeans, sunflower, cotton and peanuts.
Eligible wood products included utility poles, railroad ties, plywood, lumber, veneer, oriented strand board, particle board, fiberboard and laminated lumber.oducts.
Feed grains eligible were barley, malting barley, white and yellow corn, sorghum and oats.
Dairy products eligible were butter, butter oil, ghee, anhydrous milk fat, nonfat and whole milk powder, whey protein concentrate, lactose, nonsweetened condensed milk, fluid milk and cheese.
